newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates down, spots mostly up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates down, spots mostly up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed down across the board on Friday in very dull trading mainly due to sharp falls in fund demand ahead of the weekend, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract fell sharply to 7.11 percent from 10.85 percent on Thursday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell sharply to 1.16 million lots from 2.53 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders described trading as very dull mainly because almost all institutions, including securities houses, stood on the sidelines with the approach of the weekend.
They said a lack of market-moving factors prevented institutions from trading actively, which led to the falls in both the rates and volumes.
"As there is no new A share issue early next week, trading was slow in the early-maturing contracts today," said one trader. "So the three-day and seven-day contracts fell sharply."
Traders believe both the repo rates and trading turnover would recover early next week, they said.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Friday with sporadic buying pushing prices slightly up, traders said.
The most actively traded three-year bond that matures in August 1999 fell to 110.10 yuan from 110.20 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market plunged to 206,084 lots from 681,650 lots.
Traders said volume was very thin, indicating the spot market would consolidate in the short term.
